title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

reading.body:
This incident shows a deployment operating outside the conditions it was built for. Autonomous vehicles designed to navigate normal traffic were exposed to major traffic disruptions, unplanned road closures, and extraordinary congestion that prevented them from completing their routes. The system did not have a mechanism to anticipate or handle a scenario where heavy traffic would drain batteries faster than the vehicle could reach a charging location.

No human intervention is reported to have prevented the stranding. A system operating in public streets during a major event should have had safeguards to withdraw vehicles before conditions degraded to the point of immobilization, either through monitoring traffic in advance or through thresholds that trigger repositioning when congestion reaches certain levels.

One vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks ignited on the road. It is not established whether the autonomous system detected the hazard before the vehicle ran over it, or whether human operators monitoring the vehicle could have intervened.

reports.title: Waymo cars stranded on San Francisco streets as Fourth of July gridlock drains batteries

summary:
During Fourth of July celebrations in San Francisco on Saturday, multiple Waymo autonomous vehicles became stranded and had to be towed after their batteries drained while stuck in heavy traffic following fireworks displays near the Golden Gate Bridge. Video footage showed at least a dozen stationary Waymo vehicles, primarily Jaguar I-PACE models, lined up on streets filled with congestion. The company attributed the situation to major traffic disruptions, high traveler volume, and unplanned road closures. Additionally, one Waymo vehicle caught fire after driving over fireworks that someone had ignited on the road, though no injuries were reported.

The incident prompted frustrated responses from stranded motorists, with some waiting nearly two hours as Waymo vehicles blocked roadways. Mayor Daniel Lurie's office announced plans to discuss the traffic situation with stakeholders to improve future events. Waymo stated it is evaluating ways to strengthen its resilience during major traffic disruptions. This represents another operational challenge for the company, following a December incident when more than 100,000 customers lost power and some Waymo vehicles stopped at intersections with nonworking traffic lights.
